assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only konosuba:demon-king@original-light-novel#scoped-cohort-monograph, the active_provisional KONOSUBA_DEMON_KING_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the MAIN17 final confrontation (U013 court and Eris's qualified assessments; U014 dungeon fight, negotiation and death), with the U015 epilogue and the separately attributed U016 creator afterword, all reached through Kazuma's narration, the king's printed speech and others' testimony. The KonoSuba CURRENT_STATE_AND_CORPUS_MAP.md and the cohort 49 evidence index row were read for method, authority order and scope only. The cohort 49 audits, provenance and gate records, other monographs (including the generals'), ledgers and the Japanese source are not curated evidence on this subject and nothing is borrowed from them. No image, whole-edition, independent-reader or primary-source inspection is included.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: The single MAIN17 final confrontation, from the throne-room court (U013122) through the dungeon fight to his death after Explosion (U014496), with Aqua's report of Kazuma's death and Eris's confirmation of his defeat (U014539/667) and the U015 epilogue as reported consequences. Eris's earlier forecasts (U013246/343-353/537) are planning statements, not states of the king. His history, the war's reason, the name's origin and any earlier reign are withheld and outside this assessment; no default state exists before U013 or after his death, and no in-world calendar time is fixed.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph names status-sensitive engagement, selective retaliation, resource conservation and danger-sensitive bargaining only as explanatory hypotheses, states that their triggers overlap with ordinary command and survival incentives, and withholds a model and rule inventory. The attack after Kazuma's compound provocation (U01453-66) is explicitly not isolated to grief, pride, threat estimate or annoyance. That supports bounded canon questions about one encounter, not a motive hierarchy.

Within one encounter the monograph orders located shifts: court authority and the bluff appraisal of Megumin (U013122-135/528-540), diagnosis of the delay plan (U01413-51), retaliation (U01453-66), retreats and the aged-supporter account (U014184-221), reassessment and the stronger golem (U014235-263), brief sympathy (U014248), and the bargaining change when Explosion is shown (U014439-465). This is an intra-encounter sequence ending in death, not a developmental trajectory.

Located printed functions: elevated 我 and direct 貴様 in challenges and rebukes, the aged-supporter complaint (U014221), practical resource explanations, the grievance list, sympathy (U014248), the comparatively conversational 私 self-introduction (U014367), the withholding turn and enjoyment of irritating Kazuma (U014385/388) and the history offer as bargaining (U014472). The monograph disclaims an exhaustive idiolect, a rule that he always sounds archaic, acoustic adequacy and a Japanese performance grade.

The monograph states there is no direct ordinary domestic scene; the cherished handkerchief is graded as attachment under RELATIONSHIP_CONDITIONING, and resource choices are combat conduct. No ordinary-life repertoire is established, which is not evidence that he lacks one.

Differentiated conduct toward Kazuma as dismissed challenger, shared-complaint interlocutor and bargaining counterpart (U01413-51, U014238-248, U014439-465); Megumin as an appraised bluffer (U013528-540); his daughter only through the handkerchief and his report of its origin (U014100-112); and his generals through attributed grievances (U014277-279). Each relation rests on one encounter, the daughter has no voice, and rapport is an event rather than the end of antagonism.

There is no focalization through the king; the narrator explicitly leaves alternative reasons for his anger (U014108-112), and his specialization and grievances are spoken accounts. The swallow at Explosion is narrated bodily response, graded under CONFLICT_BEHAVIOR. No interior model is established.

The densest dimension, still one encounter: diagnosis of the delay strategy and contested duel convention (U01413-51), retaliation after compound provocation (U01453-66), mana-conserving retreats and the Inferno (U014184-221), an effective strengthened golem after setbacks (U014235-263), class-based inference that fails against Explosion (U014446-453) and successive bargaining moves under concrete danger (U014439-465). The monograph states a single encounter cannot discriminate a personal risk mechanism from ordinary adaptation to danger.

Located stances only: managerial judgments of his generals' misconduct (U014277-279, attributed and possibly self-serving), the conditional proposal to take Kazuma as a subordinate under a nonbetrayal curse (U014415-418), and offers of escape qualified by the warning that he might kill Kazuma face to face (U014343/398/433). No deliberation is shown, the reason for the war is specifically absent, and the monograph rejects both a redemptive hidden motive and acquittal through family attachment.

His own play is located once: he teases the withheld explanation, turns it back into a challenge and explicitly enjoys having irritated Kazuma in return (U014385/388); he also detects a spell-name joke (U014446-453), which the monograph limits to that detection. No repertoire is established.

One connected confrontation across MAIN17 U013-U014, with the U015 epilogue and a separately attributed U016 afterword, reached through Kazuma's narration and others' testimony; the curated item is a bounded cohort monograph, not new whole-book primary reading, and the king's history is withheld by the work itself.

Affirmative located countercases: accurate diagnosis of Kazuma's plan against a too-angry-to-think reading (U01413-66); correct reading of the borrowed blade against his misidentification of the charm as a curse (U01472-89, U014284-322) against omniscience; a real leg wound and limp against invulnerability (U014119-166); and his failed expectation about an Adventurer using Explosion (U014446-453). They are one project's adjudication of one encounter.

Claims are bound to unit and paragraph locators; Eris's forecasts (U013246/343-353/537) are kept apart from performed choices, unperformed offers from actions (U014343/398/415-418/433), the incomplete カース at U014477 from a completed spell, and the U016 afterword from in-story knowledge. There is no default state or knowledge cutoff beyond the encounter.

scenario_readiness.note: The monograph supports a contextual printed-voice account sensitive to phrasing and social stance within one encounter, and states that simulations reproducing grandiose titles would miss his practical questioning, sympathy and uncertain negotiation; it establishes no idiolect for new lines. Located forms can check a proposed line for contradiction.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: The MAIN17 final confrontation, U013122 to his death at U014496, with the bargaining posture at U014439-472 the last attested state.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Kazuma as hostile challenger and bargaining counterpart; Megumin, Eris, Mitsurugi and the throne-room retainers as enemies or subordinates; his daughter and generals only as reported absent parties.
setting_constraints: The Demon King's throne room and the dungeon to which Kazuma transports him, under mortal threat
No earlier reign, domestic setting, history, war reason or uncurated evidence
Printed Japanese only, no performed voice

scenario_readiness.note: The monograph states the tale supplies no discriminating tests across the unfamiliar contexts a generative model would need, and his offers and promises are never tested. A novel situation inside the scope can be checked against located conduct, not predicted.
No ordinary social scene is narrated; nothing is established either way.

Located stances exist, but the monograph states that no settled private value hierarchy or tested promise of safe conduct is available and that the war's reason is absent; inventing a motive would be invention.
Nothing romantic is established; a daughter implies no romantic evidence, which neither supports nor denies readiness.

Court authority, a self-described support specialization (U014221), resource management and managerial grievances (U014277-279) are located in one emergency, but the monograph withholds a model and the grievances are attributed memory; no procedure for his conduct as ruler or commander in another situation follows.

known_limits.statement: Eris's forecasts of Teleport and duel conduct, and her qualified assessments of poison resistance and instant-death ineffectiveness (MAIN17U013246/343-353/537), are informed planning statements, not performed choices or tested traits; Kazuma's later less-qualified retelling does not replace their modality.

His offers of escape, rest and monster recruitment, the imagined return with his daughter and the nonbetrayal-curse subordinate proposal (U014343/398/415-418/433) are never performed or tested; neither their sincerity nor their deceptiveness is established.

Yasaka Kyōichi (八坂恭一) is an adversary's self-introduction (U014358/367); he calls himself a demon, knows Japan only by rumor and withholds the name's origin and the war's reason (U014373/376-390), which the U016 afterword confirms remain unresolved. No Japanese-human, reincarnated, former-hero or descendant identity may be inferred.

His local enhancement of a servant or golem, the seal Eris discusses, and the weakening of the world's monsters after his death are three separate mechanisms (U013324/389; U014221/259-263; U01525; U01616) and do not combine into one buff rule.

His reports of Beldia, Vanir, Wiz, Hans, Sylvia, Serena and Wolbach are attributed, potentially selective institutional memories (U014277-279), not newly witnessed events or confirmations of those subjects' monographs.

No domestic scene, private value hierarchy, full history, verified genealogy, comparable low-stakes dispute or voice of the daughter is available; missing support is not evidence that any trait or capacity is absent.
The cohort 49 audits, provenance and gate records, ledgers, other monographs and the Japanese source are not curated on this subject and were not assessed.
